paper_title: SWE-bench: Can Language Models Resolve Real-World GitHub Issues?
core_problem: Language models have outpaced existing evaluation methods and need a challenging, sustainable testbed for frontier capabilities. Real-world software engineering is proposed as such a testbed, requiring models to resolve real GitHub issues by editing codebases, coordinating changes across multiple functions, classes and files, interacting with execution environments, processing extremely long contexts and performing complex reasoning beyond traditional code generation.
methodology_summary: Introduce SWE-bench, an evaluation framework of 2,294 software engineering problems drawn from real GitHub issues and corresponding pull requests across 12 popular Python repositories. Given a codebase and an issue description, a language model is tasked with editing the codebase to address the issue. To evaluate open models, supervised fine-tuning is performed on 7B and 13B CodeLlama-Python models to create SWE-Llama specialized repository editors that can run on consumer hardware. Retrieval for context is examined with BM25 versus an oracle retrieval setting, with context limits e.g., 27,000 tokens.
datasets_eval: SWE-bench consisting of 2,294 software engineering problems from real GitHub issues and pull requests across 12 popular Python repositories. Evaluation uses the issue description plus codebase context and verifies generated edits by running unit tests. Retrieval analysis compares BM25 retrieval to oracle retrieval for providing relevant files within token limits.
empirical_results: Both state-of-the-art proprietary models and the fine-tuned SWE-Llama can resolve only the simplest issues. Best-performing model Claude 2 solves a mere 1.96% of the issues. BM25 retrieval vs oracle: approximately 40% of instances BM25 retrieves a superset of the oracle files for the 27,000-token context limit, but in almost half of the instances with the 27,000-token limit it retrieves none of the files from the oracle context.
explicit_limitations: Existing coding benchmarks such as HumanEval mostly involve self-contained problems solvable in a few lines of code, unlike repository-wide edits. At time of writing only CodeLlama models can handle the very long contexts necessary; off-the-shelf CodeLlama variants are not capable of following detailed instructions to generate repository-wide code edits and typically output placeholder responses or unrelated code. BM25 retrieval is limited, retrieving no oracle files in almost half of instances under a 27,000-token limit. Benchmarking open models alongside proprietary models remains important.
